newsitem.title: CANADA: Solv-Ex application in final stages - Alberta.
newsitem.headline: Solv-Ex application in final stages - Alberta.

text.p: Controversial U.S. firm Solv-Ex Corp has environmental approvals for testing its bitumen extraction equipment and is in the final stages of its application to go ahead with production, the Alberta government said on Thursday.

"The department understands that presently Solv-Ex is testing their equipment, which is a standard operating procedure. This requires the company to produce some bitumen," Parker Hogan, spokesman for Alberta's Environmental Protection ministry, said.
"They will not be going into full production mode until they get approval on an amended application which is currently before Alberta Environmental Protection, and that's in its final review stages."
Hogan said the final review was expected to take less than a month.

On Wednesday, New York-based Asensio & Company Inc issued a news release quoting the department's land reclamation director, Larry Brocke, as confirming Alberta had not granted Solv-Ex a permit or any authorization to start production at its oil sands project located north of Fort McMurray, Alberta.

The news release from Asensio, an acknowledged short-seller of Solv-Ex stock, also called into question the Albuquerque, N.M.-based company's technology for cheaply extracting bitumen from oil sands on its northern Alberta leases.
Solv-Ex said early this week that production had started at its new plant.
But Asensio said the plant as it stood did not use any of Solv-Ex's own extraction technology and that "bitumen produced in this manner does not validate the 'patented Solv-Ex technology.'
"We confirm our strong sell recommendation based on our belief that shares of Solv-Ex's common stock are grossly overvalued and will soon trade well below $2 per share," Asensio said.

Hogan said Alberta Environmental Protection, whose offices in Edmonton were deluged with calls from investors after the news release was issued, was planning to issue a statement to clarify Asensio's comments as they related to the Alberta government.
"It's not the government's job to promote, one way or the other, any company," he said. "But it is our job to make sure the facts are understood."
Solv-Ex stock on Nasdaq was down 3/8 on Thursday at 11-3/4 with 144,100 shares changing hands.
